readings.passage: Last summer, I went on an unforgettable trip to Italy with my family. We were excited to explore the country's tourism attractions, from historic cities to coastal villages. Our main goal was to attend a traditional festival in a small town, known for its music and food. The journey started smoothly, but we faced a temporary issue when our train was delayed at the platform. The delay was due to a technical fault, and we had to wait for an hour. During this time, we met some friendly locals who told us about the festival. When we finally arrived, the event was in full swing. We enjoyed the performances and tried various dishes. Unfortunately, my camera was damaged when I dropped it, so I missed capturing some moments. Despite this minor problem, the trip was amazing, and I learned a lot about Italian culture. I hope to return someday for another adventure.

readings.passage: Greenfield Community Centre is hosting a leisure fair this Saturday from 10 am to 4 pm. The event aims to be a peaceful gathering for the whole community. Activities will be divided into indoor and outdoor zones, including sports, games, and creative workshops. To prevent any safety issues, we have arranged for volunteers to monitor the areas. Local businesses are welcome to set up stalls to showcase their goods. Food and drinks will be sold by local vendors. The current situation is that we need more helpers for the morning shift, especially at the button-making craft station. Left-hand scissors and tools will be available for those who need them. Please register online or at the centre by Friday to confirm your attendance. We look forward to a fun and relaxing day for everyone. Don't miss this chance to connect with your neighbours.

readings.passage: Lucy, a 16-year-old from a small town, loved skateboarding after school. Her daily routine was simple: homework, then skateboarding in the park with friends. One Saturday, while waiting for her friend at the drugstore, she bought a lottery ticket on a whim. A week later, the result was surprising – she won £10,000! Lucy was thrilled but also horrified by the sudden attention from everyone in town. She promised to use the money wisely for her family, who were not wealthy. This win was a significant development for them. Lucy still enjoys skateboarding, and she often wears her favourite sleeveless jacket while skating. Her ability to stay calm and her fitness from the sport helped her handle the situation well. The story shows how a small change in routine can lead to magnificent outcomes.

readings.passage: 10th May Today was our school science fair. I worked on my physics project about electricity. I made a poster and put an advertisement on the school noticeboard to attract visitors. My friend Tom helped me carry the heavy equipment; he's very strong, like a hotel porter! The judges were impressed. One of them, a famous scientist from the city university, asked me lots of questions. I was nervous but I explained my report clearly. Afterwards, I felt hungry. I went to the café and had a yogurt with some spinach – not my favourite, but it's healthy! It started raining heavily at lunchtime. I was so glad I remembered my umbrella. I walked home slowly, thinking about my project. I hope I win a prize. It would be great for my university account.

readings.passage: Last Saturday, our school hosted its annual Spring Fair in the main hall and playground. The event aimed to raise money for a local charity, and it was definitely a big success, raising over £500 with over 200 people attending. One of the most popular stalls was selling delicious homemade chocolate biscuits and cakes. Many visitors said these treats were the best part of the day. Another attraction was a craft table where children could decorate candles with stickers and paint. This was very popular, and some kids even made multiple candles to take home. Additionally, a local farm brought in several gentle rabbits for a petting session, which was loved by younger children, though one parent made a complaint about the noise level. To improve future events, the organisers sold tickets online before the fair, which helped reduce waiting times. They also plan to multiply the number of volunteers next year to handle the crowd better. Overall, the Spring Fair was a wonderful community event that brought everyone together.
